extra.message: User-controlled GraphQL argument 'filter' is interpolated via %-formatting directly into a raw SQL fragment passed to sqlalchemy text(): result.filter(text("title = '%s' or content = '%s'" % (filter, filter))). An attacker can inject a payload such as "aaa ' or 1=1--" to bypass filters and dump arbitrary data (confirmed by tests/test_vulnerabilities.py test_sql_injection).

ImportPaste mutation builds a shell command from user-controlled GraphQL arguments (scheme, host, port, path): cmd = helpers.run_cmd(f'curl --insecure {url}'), where run_cmd executes os.popen() (core/helpers.py:9). The hard-mode sanitizer strip_dangerous_characters only removes ';' and '&', leaving '|', '$()', backticks and newlines usable. Allows arbitrary OS command execution (confirmed by tests/test_vulnerabilities.py test_os_injection).

ImportPaste lets an unauthenticated attacker supply arbitrary scheme/host/port/path, causing the server to issue a curl request to any internal or external address and store/return the response body. No allow-list or internal-address filtering exists. Classic server-side request forgery enabling internal network scanning and cloud metadata access.

systemDiagnostics passes the user-supplied 'cmd' argument to helpers.run_cmd (os.popen). The only guard, security.allowed_cmds (core/security.py:33-39), returns True unconditionally in easy mode, and check_creds relies on a weakly-guarded admin password ('changeme'). Also note allowed_cmds has a tuple bug ('ps' 'whoami' concatenated) and startswith checks are trivially bypassed (e.g. 'echo x; id'). Results in arbitrary OS command execution (confirmed by test_os_injection_alt).

systemDebug is unauthenticated and concatenates the user-controlled 'arg' argument into a shell command: helpers.run_cmd('ps {}'.format(arg)). An attacker can supply '; id' or '| id' to execute arbitrary commands via os.popen (core/helpers.py:9).

run_cmd(cmd) executes its argument with os.popen(cmd).read(). It is the sink reached by three attacker-controlled flows: ImportPaste (core/views.py:211), systemDiagnostics (core/views.py:345), and systemDebug (core/views.py:352). Any string reaching this function is executed as a shell command.

save_file() opens WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename with no sanitization. 'filename' comes directly from the unauthenticated UploadPaste GraphQL mutation (core/views.py:185-186). A filename such as '../../app.py' or an absolute path allows arbitrary file write/overwrite on the server, potentially leading to remote code execution.

get_identity() decodes the JWT with verify_signature=False and verify_exp=False. resolve_me (core/views.py:283-296) trusts the resulting 'identity' claim, so an attacker can forge an unsigned/expired token claiming identity 'admin' and impersonate any user, including reading the admin password via UserObject.resolve_password.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: Flask SECRET_KEY and JWT_SECRET_KEY are hardcoded to the weak string 'dvga' in source. Anyone with the source can forge session cookies and sign valid JWT access/refresh tokens, fully defeating authentication.

The seeded admin account always gets the hardcoded weak password 'changeme' (random_password returns only that value), and the operator account gets 'password123' (setup.py:64). These credentials grant command execution via systemDiagnostics.

User passwords are stored as plain strings with no hashing (db.Column(db.String(60))). Login (core/views.py:234) compares plaintext passwords directly via filter_by(username=username, password=password). Database compromise or the password-disclosure resolver exposes all credentials in cleartext.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: UserObject.resolve_password returns the real plaintext password whenever info.context.json['identity'] == 'admin'. That identity value is derived from an unverified JWT (core/helpers.py:21) and from attacker-controllable request JSON, so any unauthenticated attacker can retrieve every user's cleartext password.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: EditPaste.mutate performs no authentication or ownership check: any anonymous user can modify the title/content of any paste by supplying its id (Paste.query.filter_by(id=id).update(...)). Broken object-level authorization / IDOR.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: DeletePaste.mutate deletes any paste by id with no authentication or ownership check (Paste.query.filter_by(id=id).delete()). Anonymous users can destroy arbitrary data.

resolve_delete_all_pastes wipes the entire pastes table (Paste.query.delete()) with no authentication. Because it is a Query field (not a mutation), it can also be triggered via a simple GET request to /graphql?query=..., making it CSRF-able as well.
resolve_read_and_burn reads and permanently deletes any 'burn' paste by id with no authentication, allowing anonymous data theft and destruction.

resolve_paste fetches pastes by id or title without checking the 'public' flag, so private pastes (e.g. the seeded 'My Phone Number' paste) are readable by anyone who enumerates ids. Similarly resolve_search (lines 298-312) returns private pastes regardless of visibility.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: resolve_audits returns the full audit log (all GraphQL queries/operations executed by every user) with no authentication. The /audit HTML route (lines 426-429) exposes the same data. Leaks sensitive operational data; the regex-based redaction in clean_query (core/models.py:25-28) only masks inline token/password literals and is easily bypassed via variables.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: format_custom_error embeds full Python stack traces (traceback.format_stack, traceback.format_exc) and the absolute server file path into GraphQL error responses returned to clients. Aids attackers in mapping the server internals (confirmed by tests/test_vulnerabilities.py test_stack_trace_errors).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: simulate_load() sleeps in a loop up to 500 iterations x 0.1s (~50 seconds) per call. It is invoked by the unauthenticated systemUpdate query (core/views.py:332-335), letting a single anonymous request tie up a worker thread for ~50s and enabling trivial denial of service. The cost middleware is disabled in easy mode and trivially bypassed.

sys.setrecursionlimit(100000) drastically raises the recursion limit so deeply nested GraphQL queries (circular fragments) drive the Python interpreter into C-stack exhaustion and crash the process instead of raising RecursionError — a deliberate denial-of-service weakness.

The /graphql endpoint is registered with batch=True, allowing arbitrarily large arrays of queries in a single HTTP request (batch DoS / query amplification) with no batch-size limit, compounding the missing depth/cost protections in easy mode.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Stored XSS: paste title, content, owner name, IP and userAgent (the latter two attacker-controlled via the HTTP User-Agent header at paste creation, core/views.py:125) are interpolated into HTML template literals and inserted with jQuery $(pasteHTML).prependTo(...) without escaping. The same pattern recurs in get_pastes() at lines 132-156. Any stored <script> in a paste executes in every viewer's browser.

The before_request handler lets any client downgrade the global security mode to 'easy' (or per-request via the X-DVGA-MODE header), instantly disabling depth/cost/introspection/deny-list/operation-name protections and command sanitization for everyone. The /difficulty/<level> route (lines 441-451) does the same without authentication. Security controls are entirely client-controllable.

IGQLProtectionMiddleware gates GraphiQL access solely on the client-supplied 'env' cookie equal to 'graphiql:enable'. Any attacker can set this cookie themselves to bypass the access restriction — authorization enforced client-side.

The /start_over route is unauthenticated and invokes helpers.initialize(), which shells out to 'python3 setup.py' (core/helpers.py:11-12), deleting and rebuilding the entire database and upload directory. Anonymous users can destroy all application data at will (denial of service / data destruction).

resp.set_cookie('env', 'graphiql:disable') sets a security-relevant cookie without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes, leaving it accessible to JavaScript (combined with the stored XSS in paste.html) and modifiable by the client to bypass the GraphiQL gate.
